reproduction: Existing native receipts record exact small-field reduction tests, characteristic-power descent, signed cancellations and huge binary multiplicities. The tests do not execute the large auxiliary-prime branch or prove the zero-free theorem.
reconciliation: Sparse complexity is polynomial in sparse input, total degree of distinct densely returned factors and binary multiplicities. Construction complexity is polynomial in dense output length.

Corollary 3 explicitly uses family 142 Theorem 1.1. Its Theorem 1.2 takes auxiliary primes only in the large-characteristic branch, with dependence on numerical sizes. The independent algebraic review checked splitter, norm and divisor steps, degree-decreasing table recursion and uniform bounds.

For every prime q≤n and p>B^200000, p ∤ 12q and X^q−p is Eisenstein at p in F=Q(μ_12q). The Kummer extension is cyclic of degree q. Its characters are finite-order Hecke characters on exactly a cyclotomic F containing μ_12, and the companion strip Re(s)>1−10^−6 permits the principal pole and has no conductor or height cutoff. It restores incomplete factors, whose zeros lie at Re(s)=0.

Abelian zeta factorization supplies the strip to both zeta functions. Family 142 proves its own uniform smoothed explicit formula with error O(x^(1−δ)(log discriminant+degree)), so per-field proof constants of the companion are immaterial. Degree/discriminant bounds O(B^3) and x=TB^20,000,000 give relative error O(T^−δ B^−17). Higher powers and ramified primes cannot account for the main positive difference. Completely split primes cancel, so the necessary auxiliary prime exists within the claimed size; sequential trial division is polynomial at that size.
The family 142 fixed exponent fits within the loose bound printed in Corollary 3. No Dirichlet-only or Lean theorem is used.
